# the contributor audit: simultaneous prescribed-mass vertex trims


`candidate a277c91b06544c90`, with
its stated equal-slope requirement for the linear dual and its
separate dimension-one rule. This is a necessary variational
condition, not a below-target descent theorem.

I read the full source. Each polytope vertex lies in an original
measured fiber. Strict exposure gives a bounded truncated tangent
cone and a positive support gap to every other fiber. The local
removed volume is exactly a_v t_v^d. Choosing the stated powers
therefore prescribes the removed masses exactly. Distinct vertex
neighborhoods are disjoint for a cutoff uniform over the finite
probability simplex. Intersecting all ambient halfspaces preserves
actual compatibility, and every original positive fiber survives.

The fixed cap incidences are exact, including the tangent-cone
fraction when a cap passes through the vertex. For d>=2, projecting
each shrinking deletion onto the cap hyperplane bounds interaction
with an O(epsilon) threshold movement by
O(epsilon t_v^(d-1)). Summing gives a uniform o(epsilon) estimate.
This justifies the nonsmooth quantile inverse, with the original
distinct right/left section slopes retained. Negative weighted
responses at all selected deepest bases yield closed whole-fiber
covers of strictly cheaper mass. Nondeep finite gaps persist.

Under equal slopes the explicit threshold velocities have weighted
sum zero and every cap in a circuit has the same first-order mass.
The upper comparison for the actual maximum therefore has the
claimed slope, without differentiating any optimizing center.
Separation of the compact column hull from the open upper orthant
gives a nonnegative nonzero dual vector. Its normalized sum is one,
and its bound on every column is exactly the stated finite dual.
The reverse implication is immediate by averaging. All quantifiers
are correctly per circuit selection, not one universal stress.

At optimal primal and dual solutions, each supported column lies
in the same dual affine hyperplane. The augmented column vectors
(1,A_v) therefore have rank at most the number of rows. A linear
dependence of more supported columns preserves the total weight
and every payoff; shifting to a zero weight reduces support.
This proves the support bound including equality cases.

For the explicit protected-layer source, the exposing planes have
gap at least one at every other integer fiber, so t<=1 trims exactly
the intended corner simplex. The layer-isolating critical circuits
have equal reciprocal-section weights1/3. Their incidence matrix
is(2/3)I, whose exact value2/(3L) exceeds beta1/(2L); no single
column is profitable. The three finite cap masses, their cover,
the normalized decrement, and the retained no-heavy inequality
are algebraically correct. One deletion alone has the stated exact
increased depth because another layer supplies the lower bound
and the old median covers supply the upper bound.

The d1 endpoint rule explicitly keeps the min/max interaction and
does not import the d>=2 small-slab estimate. The fixed-N-plane
restriction is also kept separate from the unrestricted class.
The simplex-product calibration correctly prevents interpreting
the incidence game as an automatic sharp-constant proof.

The independent exact verifier returned PASS for20 actual multiple-
plane source/cap constructions,324 all-dimensional decrement and
no-heavy identities, and128 rational primal-dual/support checks.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
